Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading syllables (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learn
Topic 2.2: Reading three letter words
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading three letter words, part of Reading 2.1 Reading syllables (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub strand the learn in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to know how to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading three letter words together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: The learner together with others practise reading three letter words.

• Integrity: The learner exercises discipline in taking turns as they blend sounds and read syllables.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Why is it important to know how to read?

Core competencies:

• Self –efficacy: The learner reads syllables accurately and independently.

• Learning to learn: The learner persists and pursues reading syllables correctly.

Values:

• Unity: The learner together with others practise reading three letter words.

• Integrity: The learner exercises discipline in taking turns as they blend sounds and read syllables.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Effective communication: Reading of syllables is a skill that prepares learners to communicate by way of writing.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Ability to read is necessary in every Activity Area and so the skill to read cuts across all other Activity Areas.
